industry: Medicare (licensed agents/brokers/TPMOs and plans: Medicare Advantage, Part D, Medicare Supplement/Medigap)
words_and_claims_to_avoid: Anything implying government endorsement or connection: 'Official', 'Medicare Notice', 'Benefits update', 'Federal benefit information', Capitol/eagle/flag/seal imagery, red-white-blue notice styling, Medicare card facsimiles (42 USC 1320b-10; 39 USC 3001(h); 42 CFR 422.2262). A 'not affiliated' footer does NOT cure it.
Using a Medicare card image without CMS authorization (gold 006/007 mock cards).

'Free' to describe a $0 premium, reduced premium or reduced cost-sharing (422.2262). 'MY SERVICE IS FREE!' (gold 007) is about the agent's service: OK only if accurate and not confused with plan costs.
Claims that CMS or Medicare endorses or recommends you; implying an MA plan is a Medicare supplement; implying plans are only for seniors.
Fake or invented deadlines, 'respond within 5 days', 'final notice' (CMS 'mislead or confuse'; MMR-513 negative example).

Plan-specific benefit numbers ($0 premium, '$X dental', Part B giveback) unless the piece is filed/approved through the plan as marketing with all required disclaimers (gold 013 'plans from $0 premium').
Cash, gift cards that work like cash (Visa/Amazon/Walmart) or gifts over nominal value ($15/item, $75/year per OIG); any gift conditioned on enrolling.
Meals at marketing events (only at educational events); 'free dinner & door prizes' sales seminars (gold 017 Ballo).
Non-health products (annuities, life) cross-sold in Medicare appointments; superlatives you can't support if CMS asks.
Frail, lonely, hospital-bed imagery as default; sepia nostalgia (MMR-523).
compliance_notes: 42 CFR 422.2260-2274 (MA) and 423.2260-2274 (Part D) govern communications and marketing; TPMOs (agents/brokers/FMOs) are covered. CY2027 final rule CMS-4212-F (91 FR 17583, Apr 6 2026) applies to marketing from Oct 1 2026.

TPMO disclaimer required in print marketing (422.2267(e)(41)), current wording: 'We do not offer every plan available in your area. Currently we represent [insert number of organizations] organizations which offer [insert number of plans] products in your area. Please contact Medicare.gov or 1-800-MEDICARE to get information on all of your options.' (SHIP reference removed by CMS-4212-F). Use the variant for TPMOs representing all organizations if applicable.

422.2264 unsolicited contact: unsolicited direct mail is allowed; door-to-door, cold calls, texts, voicemails, DMs and calls to confirm receipt of mail are not. A returned reply card (BRC) makes a callback solicited; scope-of-appointment (SOA) and BRC permission valid 12 months. CMS-4212-F removed the 48-hour wait between SOA and appointment and allows SOA collection at educational events.

Events: educational events must be advertised as educational and can't market plans; marketing events may follow an educational event (CY2027) with notice and a chance to leave; no meals at marketing events; no required sign-in sheets; raffle info used only for the raffle.

Gifts: nominal value only per OIG ($15/item, $75/year aggregate in OIG's policy statement), offered to everyone regardless of enrollment, never cash or cash equivalents; promotional items need the 'no obligation to enroll' disclaimer (422.2267(e)(37)). A blog claims the 2026 MCMG raised this to $17/$85 - unverified; confirm against current CMS guidance.
Customer service numbers must show hours of operation and TTY in the same size; if 1-800-MEDICARE appears, include its hours (24/7).
No unsolicited materials referencing the MA OEP (Jan 1-Mar 31) to MA enrollees (422.2263).
Agency/organization name at least 12-pt, not hidden; testimonials only from actual enrollees, paid endorsements/actors disclosed (422.2262).

Medigap is state-regulated: Medicare Supplement ads follow NAIC Model 660 as adopted; many states require filing ads with the commissioner (Model 660 contemplates filing at least 30 days before use where the commissioner requires review).
42 USC 1320b-10: up to $5,000 per violation, each mail piece separate. Iowa consent judgments (MMR-527/528) show enforcement against government-lookalike senior mail.
standing_rules: Emotion-agnostic: fear, joy, pride, status, relief, nostalgia are all options; the client chooses.
Every angle and combo carries a sell-the-outcome line.
Unverified (agency/vendor-only) results are labeled; never quote them as fact on a card.
No age/demographic angle unless a cited source supports it for this industry; even then, check Fair Housing / ECOA before using it in housing or credit.

Medicare-specific: fear is allowed only when the fact is true and current (e.g., real late-enrollment penalties, real AEP dates) and paired with a clear free step; CMS bans anything that misleads or confuses, so never manufacture urgency.

emotion_by_offer.why: IEP is a legal 7-month window; penalties are real; most people want a clear plan.
headline_offer_patterns: 'New to Medicare? Start with a free checklist.'
'Medicare can be confusing. It doesn't have to be.' (gold 002/016)
emotion_by_offer.what_backfires: Mock Medicare cards, government styling, invented deadlines, maze/puzzle clip art that reinforces confusion without relief (gold 014/018 - fine as a device only if the offer resolves it).

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Humana 'official' look lifted response +24% (MMR-520, agency) vs 42 USC 1320b-10 / 39 USC 3001(h) / Iowa enforcement (MMR-527/528)
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Law wins: important-looking own-brand design is fine; no government cues of any kind.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Gold 017 'free dinner & door prizes' seminar (44 attendees, 33 clients, vendor) vs 422.2263 no meals at marketing events
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Law wins: meals only at educational events; marketing events get no meal, and gifts stay nominal.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Gold 006/007 mock Medicare card graphics vs 422.2262 and 42 USC 1320b-10
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Law wins: no card facsimile without CMS authorization.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Repo synthesis TPMO wording ('Any information we provide is limited to those plans...') vs current eCFR 422.2267(e)(41) wording
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Current regulation wins: use the eCFR text with organization/plan counts; SHIP reference removed for CY2027.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Patrick's emotion-agnostic rule (fear OK) vs CMS 'mislead or confuse' standard
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Both apply: fear is allowed when it's a true, current fact (penalties, real dates) with a clear free step; manufactured urgency or scare framing that confuses is out.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Secondary blog claims a $17/$85 nominal gift cap vs OIG policy statement $15/$75
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Verified primary source wins until CMS/OIG text confirms a change: use $15/$75.
